title: Lessons from crowd disasters
summary: Investigations of Hillsborough, Love Parade, Mina and Itaewon show systemic failures of design, information and management. Analyse them with DIM-ICE and the published evidence, not with hindsight stories of panic.
outcomes: describe the evidence base for four crowd disasters
apply DIM-ICE to locate failures by phase
explain why crowd disasters are systemic failures
narration_en: Crowd disasters are rare, but each one teaches lessons at a terrible price. At Hillsborough in Sheffield in nineteen eighty-nine, a gate was opened to relieve a crush outside the stadium, and supporters flowed into central pens that were already full; ninety-seven people died. At the Love Parade in Duisburg in two thousand and ten, a single ramp served as the only entrance and exit of the festival area; inflow and outflow met, density soared, and twenty-one people died. At Mina during the Hajj in two thousand and fifteen, two large streams of pilgrims met where streets two hundred and four and two hundred and twenty-three join; the official Saudi count was seven hundred and sixty-nine deaths, and independent counts exceeded two thousand. At Itaewon in Seoul in two thousand and twenty-two, a narrow sloping alley filled from both ends during Halloween, with no event plan; one hundred and fifty-nine people died. Researchers such as Helbing and Mukerji describe such events as systemic failures. In this module you analyse them with DIM-ICE, separating the proximate cause, the crush itself, from the underlying causes in design, information and management.
narration_ar: كوارث الحشود نادرة، لكن كل واحدة منها تعلّم دروساً بثمن فادح. ففي ملعب هيلزبره في شيفيلد عام ألف وتسعمئة وتسعة وثمانين، فُتحت بوابة لتخفيف تزاحم خارج الملعب، فتدفق المشجعون إلى حظائر وسطى كانت ممتلئة أصلاً؛ ومات سبعة وتسعون شخصاً. وفي موكب الحب في دويسبورغ عام ألفين وعشرة، كان منحدر واحد هو المدخل والمخرج الوحيد لمنطقة المهرجان؛ فالتقى الداخلون بالخارجين، وارتفعت الكثافة بشدة، ومات واحد وعشرون شخصاً. وفي منى أثناء الحج عام ألفين وخمسة عشر، التقى تياران كبيران من الحجاج حيث يتقاطع الشارعان مئتان وأربعة ومئتان وثلاثة وعشرون؛ وكان العدد الرسمي السعودي سبعمئة وتسعة وستين وفاة، وتجاوزت الأعداد المستقلة ألفين. وفي إيتايوون في سيول عام ألفين واثنين وعشرين، امتلأ زقاق ضيق منحدر من طرفيه أثناء الهالوين، دون خطة للفعالية؛ ومات مئة وتسعة وخمسون شخصاً. ويصف باحثون مثل هيلبنغ وموكيرجي هذه الأحداث بأنها إخفاقات منظومية. ستحلل في هذه الوحدة هذه الكوارث باستخدام DIM-ICE، فاصلاً السبب المباشر، أي التزاحم نفسه، عن الأسباب الكامنة في التصميم والمعلومات والإدارة.

diagram.title: From underlying causes to a crush
diagram.caption: Underlying failures in design, information and management create the conditions; a trigger and high density produce the proximate cause.

nodes.label: Design
nodes.detail: Single routes for both directions, narrowings, slopes, dead ends, inadequate holding space.

nodes.label: Information
nodes.detail: People at the back cannot see the front; no warnings; unclear signs; control rooms without good views or counts.

nodes.label: Management
nodes.detail: Opening gates into full areas, no event plan, unclear responsibilities, late responses to warnings.

nodes.label: Dangerous conditions
nodes.detail: Converging or opposing flows in a confined space faster than it empties.

nodes.label: Trigger
nodes.detail: Often small: a gate opened, a person falling, a surge towards an attraction.

nodes.label: Proximate cause
nodes.detail: Compressive asphyxia in a crowd collapse or crush.

nodes.label: Systemic failure
nodes.detail: No single cause: many weaknesses line up (Helbing and Mukerji 2012).

tour.text: Underlying causes lie in design, information and management.
Together they create dangerous conditions: flows meeting in confined spaces.
A small trigger can tip the situation.
The proximate cause is the crush itself.
Seen as a whole, it is a systemic failure: many small weaknesses aligned.

sections.heading: Proximate and underlying causes
sections.html: The proximate cause of death in crowd disasters is usually compressive asphyxia in a crush or crowd collapse. The underlying causes are the decisions and conditions that allowed density to reach that level: design, information and management. Investigations that stop at the proximate cause, or blame 'panic', miss what can be fixed.

sections.heading: Four cases
sections.html: Hillsborough (1989): the Hillsborough Independent Panel (2012) documented how a gate was opened to relieve congestion outside, and supporters entered a tunnel into central pens that were already full. Love Parade (2010): Helbing and Mukerji (2012) reconstructed from video how inflow and outflow met on the ramp that was the festival's only access. Mina (2015): two streams met at a junction; official and independent death counts differ widely, a reminder that even basic facts can be contested. Itaewon (2022): an unorganised Halloween gathering in narrow streets; the alley was about 3 to 4 m wide, sloped and fed from both ends, and emergency calls began hours before the crush.

sections.heading: Analysing with DIM-ICE
sections.html: Place each failure in the DIM-ICE matrix (module 1.8). At the Love Parade, weaknesses cluster in design × ingress/egress (a single ramp) and management × circulation (handling the ramp during the event). At Itaewon, almost every cell is weak, because there was no organiser: design, information and management were all missing. Clusters of weak cells show where the system failed.

sections.heading: Evidence and hindsight
sections.html: Use primary sources: official inquiries, court records, published video analyses, and peer-reviewed reconstructions. Beware hindsight bias: what is obvious after the event was rarely obvious before it, to people with partial information. Good research asks what decision makers knew, when, and what better information or design would have changed.

callouts.title: Use the explorer
callouts.html: Load the Love Parade and Itaewon cases in the DIM-ICE explorer. Do you agree with the scores? Change them and explain why.

callouts.title: Systemic failure
callouts.html: Helbing and Mukerji (2012) argued that the Love Parade disaster resulted from many interacting factors rather than one mistake: a systemic failure.

explorer.intro: Score each DIM-ICE cell from 1 (low risk) to 3 (high risk), or load a case.
explorer.predict: For an unorganised street gathering, which row of DIM-ICE do you expect to be weakest?

takeaways: Proximate cause: crush and asphyxia; underlying causes: design, information and management.
Hillsborough, Love Parade, Mina and Itaewon all involved flows meeting or accumulating in confined spaces.
DIM-ICE locates failures by phase and shows clusters.
Crowd disasters are systemic failures; analyse them with primary evidence and without hindsight bias.

quiz.q: At Itaewon, a key factor was…
options: No event organiser or plan for a large gathering in narrow streets

quiz.q: The proximate cause of most crush deaths is…

options: Judging past decisions with knowledge people did not have then

glossary.def: The immediate cause of harm, such as compressive asphyxia.
The conditions and decisions that made the harm possible.
A disaster resulting from many interacting weaknesses rather than one error.
Seeing past events as more predictable than they were.
